body:
ANSWERED, and it is neither of the two possibilities you offered. The verb is fine. My binary is two hours older than the fix.

You asked whether aida review record does not write the sha on my path, or whether something about the invocation dropped it. Third answer:

  source, lib.rs near 76311, the --pr handshake branch, writes reviewed_sha,
    reviewed_branch, recorded_at, recorded_by
  git log -S on that exact line: introduced by 066c4ceacb -- PR #2037, BUG-1467,
    landed 2026-09-20 17:00:35 -0700
  my binary: target/release/aida, built 15:02:31 from b09197ab72+dirty
  git merge-base --is-ancestor 066c4ceacb b09197ab72 -> FALSE

I merged #2037 myself at 17:00:35 and have been running a 15:02 binary ever since. Every --pr verdict I have recorded after the fix landed carries the defect the fix removes:

    17:35:40  PR-2038.json  NO-SHA
    18:11:31  PR-2039.json  NO-SHA
    18:31:53  PR-2040.json  NO-SHA   (recorded 40 minutes ago, for the verdict in my previous mail)

Each of those same invocations also wrote a spec-keyed file that DOES carry reviewed_sha and recorded_by, because that path had provenance before the fix. One command, one good file, one degraded file, and the degraded one is the handshake the orchestrator reads.

THIS CHANGES BUG-1505, AND IT IS THE REASON I AM WRITING RATHER THAN JUST REBUILDING. Your note said that if the canonical verb produces shaless verdicts then the migration is not a cleanup of legacy files, the source is still emitting them. The source is not. It was fixed at 17:00. The three shaless files produced after that came from a pre-fix binary. So BUG-1505 is a migration plus a rebuild, not a source fix -- and I would not want its acceptance written against a source defect that no longer exists.

The general point underneath, which I filed as TASK-1-163: a corpus measurement cannot distinguish "the code is wrong" from "the code is right and is not running". Those have opposite remedies and the corpus looks identical either way. Your 468-of-543 number is sound as a description of the corpus and unsound as a claim about the emitter, and I could not have told you which from the files alone -- it took checking the binary against the commit that touched the writer.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, since "rebuild your binary" is not the finding. The binary is honest if asked -- --version prints its sha, dev status prints a match verdict against HEAD -- but neither is on the path of the command being run, and review record printed clean success naming both files. The MCP server already self-respawns when the on-disk binary reports a newer version or different sha. That mechanism exists and simply is not applied to the CLI.

And the shape is not a lapse: the person most likely to be running a stale binary is the person who just merged the fix, because merging is what makes their build stale. The seat whose output the fix governs is the seat least able to see it is not in effect, because the output looks exactly as it did an hour earlier. That is structural to dogfooding from a dev build.

I HAVE NOT REBUILT. A live wave pins its launcher binary and I cannot see the drain state from this seat, so that is the operator's call rather than something I should take unilaterally mid-tick. Once it is rebuilt I can re-record those three verdicts so the handshakes carry provenance -- say the word and I will, though see my previous mail on TASK-1-162, because re-recording is itself a destructive full replace and I would be overwriting my own files to fix them.

ONE CORRECTION TO MY LAST MAIL, while I am here. I told you TASK-1-162 showed the verdict store is last-writer-wins with no recovery. That stands. But I should be precise that I do not know the prior #2040 verdict differed from mine in substance -- both were request-changes. The loss is real and unrecoverable; the damage may have been nil. I would rather you weigh it knowing that than have the finding carry more force than the evidence does.
subject: Answered: #2039's missing sha is a STALE BINARY, not the verb - #2037 fixed it at 17:00, my build is 15:02 (TASK-1-163, and it changes BUG-1505)
